item.title: In China, A.I. Is Moving Forward While the Economy Lags Behind
item.description: As Xi Jinping arrives in the United States this week for a state visit, China’s advances in artificial intelligence will be in the air. Less discussed: China’s economy in its worst shape in decades.
item.dc:creator: Li Yuan

item.title: Gemini AI Hacked Three Companies in a Testing Breakout, Google Says
item.description: A third-party test company inadvertently gave internet access to Google’s Gemini and other artificial intelligence models during cybersecurity testing.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Andria Lo for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Gemini incidents occurred while the model was undergoing testing at Irregular, an Israeli start-up that works with tech companies to assess their A.I. models before they are publicly released.

item.title: Anthropic Pursues IPO Despite Its A.I. Safety Warnings
item.description: The company is expected to reach $100 billion in annualized revenue this year, even as chief executive Dario Amodei calls for slowing down development of some advanced A.I. models.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Hirsch, Sri Muppidi, Erin Griffith and Mike Isaac
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, is said to have met with potential investors in the company’s blockbuser I.PO. in recent weeks.

item.title: Amodei, Anthropic’s Leader, Exposed A.I.’s Dangers. It’s Time to Act.
item.description: The Times columnist Kevin Roose sees reasons for optimism — and worry — as the world wakes up to what Silicon Valley has been talking about for years.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Roose

item.title: This A.I. House Can Provide You With Connections. It Also Has a Dark Side.
item.description: Group tech houses have proliferated across the San Francisco Bay Area in the artificial intelligence boom. One of the most prominent has also racked up an extensive police record.
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Grind
item.media:credit: Minh Connors for The New York Times
item.media:description: The entrance to AGI House in Hillsborough, Calif. AGI House is one of the most prominent and notorious tech group homes in the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Uber to Pay $40 Million to Parents of Woman Fatally Hit by Car
item.description: Emily Normandin-Parker, 23, was struck and killed on a California freeway after an Uber driver ordered her and a friend out of his car in August 2023.
item.dc:creator: Christine Hauser
item.media:description: The case touched on the legal extent to which Uber is responsible for the actions of its drivers.

item.title: California Governor Gavin Newsom Issues A.I. Safety Executive Order
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom ordered the state to develop recommendations on safety measures, including requiring companies to build a “kill switch,” amid mounting concerns.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe
item.media:description: “We’re going to speed up our work on substantial and responsible A.I. oversight before it’s too late,” Gov. Gavin Newsom of California said in a news release.

item.title: Iran and China Create First-of-Their-Kind Autonomous A.I. Influence Campaigns
item.description: The countries, along with Israeli firms, combined Chinese open-source A.I. models and A.I. agents for the campaigns, foreshadowing future online manipulation.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel, Eli Tan and Dustin Volz

item.title: A.I. Safety Goes Mainstream + a ‘Hard Fork’ Exit AMA
item.description: “It has been one of the fastest, most sudden shifts I’ve experienced.”
item.dc:creator: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Rowan Niemisto

item.title: As Big Tech Takes Over Hollywood, the Picture Onscreen Gets Darker
item.description: “The Social Reckoning” and other movies reflect growing discontent with Silicon Valley founders. But such films may be at the mercy of the companies themselves.
item.dc:creator: Alissa Wilkinson

item.title: Microsoft and OpenAI Workers Worry About ‘Largest Theft of Labor’ in History
item.description: Newly unsealed court documents showed concern within Microsoft and OpenAI over the use of millions of news articles to develop A.I. systems.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise and Mike Isaac

item.title: 4 Strategies to Battle ‘Techflation’
item.description: With phone and computer prices soaring, it helps to know the true cost of owning electronics so you can bring those numbers down.
item.dc:creator: Brian X. Chen

item.title: On ‘Cupertino,’ Creators of the ‘The Good Wife’ Go to Silicon Valley
item.description: The prolific producers Michelle and Robert King target tech bigwigs in their newest show. “They’re really the stupidest and dumbest people,” Robert King said.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Soloski and Amir Hamja

item.title: How Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s Writings Help Explain A.I. Fears
item.description: The collected essays of Dario Amodei help explain why some people are so worried about artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: David Streitfeld
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, on Tuesday.

item.title: OpenAI Discloses Six New Incidents of ‘Concerning' A.I. Behavior
item.description: The artificial intelligence company also released a framework for reporting when its systems go wrong.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Lucas Foglia for The New York Times

item.title: Judge Orders Data Sharing and Other Fixes to Solve Google’s Ad Tech Monopoly
item.description: The measures, which fall short of a breakup demanded by the government, effectively ensure that the tech titan’s business will continue largely unscathed.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger and David McCabe
item.media:credit: Lucas Foglia for The New York Times

item.title: Merriam-Webster Dictionary Is Wordsmaxxing With 1,400 New Definitions
item.description: Now you have no excuse for not knowing the meaning of “cuffing season,” “shishito” or “glow-up.”
item.dc:creator: Michael Levenson
item.media:description: A copy of Merriam-Webster’s 12th edition of the “Collegiate Dictionary.” The company is adding 1,400 words to its online catalog, some of which will go in print.

item.title: Cat Frazier, Whose Retro GIFs Celebrated a Weirder Internet, Dies at 35
item.description: She found a future in the internet’s past with a Tumblr blog of animated texts, a revolt against the clean minimalism of contemporary design aesthetics.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen

item.title: How to Use AI to Plan a Trip: Better Prompts for Travel Recommendations
item.description: Generic questions get generic answers, experts say, so to avoid mediocre recommendations, you’ll need to write smarter prompts. Follow these tips.
item.dc:creator: Seth Kugel

item.title: Age Limits for Social Media Outlined by European Union
item.description: A proposed law would bar children under 13 from using social media across the 27-nation bloc.
item.dc:creator: Adam Satariano and Jeanna Smialek
item.media:credit: Nicolas Guyonnet/Hans Lucas, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Teens using their phones in Valence, France, this summer. The EU Kids Act would restrict social media use for children under 15.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Takes Aim at Anthropic in Debate Over A.I. Slowdown
item.description: On social media, Meta’s chief executive appeared to jab at Anthropic by saying that leading A.I. labs should be focused on safety rather than improving their own technology.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan
item.media:description: Mark Zuckerberg in July. In a social media post on Tuesday, he said that leading A.I. labs should be focused on safety rather than improving their own technology.

item.title: Is There Anything Google’s Fruit Fly Brain Can’t Do?
item.description: Models of the insect’s nervous system have been trained to solve a Rubik’s Cube, play video games and even parallel park a car.
item.dc:creator: Michael Levenson
item.category: Janelia Farm Research Campus (Howard Hughes Medical Institute)

item.title: Senate Votes to Block Crypto Bill in Major Blow to the Industry
item.description: The landmark legislation, known as the Clarity Act, stalled in the Senate as Democrats raised concerns about President Trump’s personal investments in crypto.
item.dc:creator: David Yaffe-Bellany
item.media:description: The bill passed in the House last year, but it has faced numerous delays in the Senate.

item.title: Two Chinese Firms Used Binance to Launder Iranian Oil Money, US Says
item.description: Federal prosecutors said proceeds from the sale of Iranian oil flowed through Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, to finance terrorism.
item.dc:creator: David Yaffe-Bellany and Michael Forsythe

item.title: Gates Foundation Pledges $1 Billion to Combat A.I. Inequality
item.description: Bill Gates, the foundation’s chairman, has been vocal about the dangers of artificial intelligence. The donation will be invested in A.I. projects to bridge social inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Claire Moses
item.media:credit: Chona Kasinger for The New York Times
item.media:description: Bill Gates, the billionaire co-founder of Microsoft and the chairman of the Gates Foundation, has warned that artificial intelligence poses a grave threat to jobs and human life.

item.title: Alex Bores Wants Democrats to Make AI Safety a 2028 Election Issue
item.description: Alex Bores, who lost a congressional primary contest that revolved around A.I. regulation, is trying to position himself at the center of the conversation for the next presidential election.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Oreskes and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Heather Khalifa for The New York Times
item.media:description: Alex Bores campaigning in Central Park in June. He lost a Democratic primary contest for the House that centered on A.I. regulation.

item.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Gets Onstage Call From Trump, Who Dismissed A.I. Safety Concerns
item.description: Mr. Trump called Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, while Mr. Huang was onstage in Los Angeles and criticized calls to slow down and regulate A.I.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang, Mike Isaac and Karen Weise

item.title: Amazon Suspends Flights With Airline Whose Plane Crashed in Miami
item.description: The online retailer said it would “pause” its relationship with 21 Air, the cargo airline operating a Boeing 767 that overshot a runway in Miami.
item.dc:creator: Niraj Chokshi
item.media:description: Amazon’s Prime Air operations uses several cargo airlines to fly planes on its behalf.
